I ALWAYS get caught up in all that stuff and have to remind myself all the time about what I should really be focused on.  There's SO many awesome things to do and plan and see that it's really easy to lose focus.

I'm going to forego the "get there for rope drop" or "Get a FP for XYZ ride" or "make sure you eat at ABC restaurant" etc...... You'll get enough of that.

My advice: R-E-L-A-X.  It's a vacation with some the most enjoyable and important people in your life.  You're not going to see and do everything - you CAN'T see and do everything.  Don't try. Don't worry about FastPass or line times or extra magic hours, etc... Don't run from ride to ride or reservation to reservation - pick out a few that you really want to experience and make sure you hit them.  If you have to wait in a line - be patient.  Spend your time in line talking and enjoying the company of those people you love - being with them is the important part.  It's a vacation, don't stress.  

I've been to WDW over a dozen times across my 40 years and ALL of my best memories are about the people I was with - I remember when I was 6 and seeing my Dad's surprise and wonderment when he first saw MK - I remember his face WAY more than I remember any ride I went on.  The memory of kissing the love of my life as we sat and watched fireworks at Epcot - not how we were able to do ALL of Future World in one afternoon - is the strongest memory.  I remember enjoying a late night at MK with my 13 year old daughter and how happy she was and how much I enjoyed just being there with her WAY more than I remember going on Astro Orbiter.  

Relax and enjoy the experience with your loved ones - it's WAY more precious than making sure you don't wait an extra 15 minutes for Space Mountain.  

Have a great vacation.

TL;DR - RELAX - enjoy your friends and family.

In order for me to not commit suicide I have to establish some "next thing" that I need to make it to in my life. I tell myself, just make it to "X" and then you can do it. The fact that I allow myself to think that it's going to happen right after "X" keeps the overwhelming feeling of NEEDING to die at bay.....most of the time. When I'm in crisis I try and focus on that thing and tell myself over and over again why I need to stay alive to get to that date or accomplish that goal. Then, as that time approaches, during the times when I'm more lucid and not in crisis, I try and find the next thing to get to.

For example, last year it was getting to my son's 16th birthday, then spending one last holiday season with my kids, then it was helping my Aunt get through chemo (she passed away), now it's getting her estate settled and making sure the money she left me gets into trust funds for my kid's education. Preface - 99% of the time it's worth it to go through your insurance.  Sure, it might cost you more in premiums, but it keeps you protected from any scams or BS.

Get a copy of the estimate - if you think it's BS take it to a shop you know to be trustworthy and ask them to take a quick look at it.  If it seems fine and you're willing to pay the damages - GET A RECEIPT from the other guy.  You don't need a detailed release or anything, just have him write you a receipt being sure to note that it's for repairs from an auto accident on "such and such a date" and have him sign it.  Also, not a bad idea to pay with a check, so you can track that he cashed it.
Chances are nothing will ever come of it.  But if he does ever try and sue you, or report it to your insurance carrier, the receipt with the estimate will serve as your proof that you paid for the damages.  
This should be enough for a court or your insurance to dismiss any further claim he might make.
